tldr: Two articles worth analytics-department time, three are mid-market romance.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Add 2-yr K% trajectory as an explicit flag on the pitcher board. Discount Q4-trajectory rentals, buy-low on Q1.
articles.what_is_missing: How does this interact with rental vs multi-year control? My pitcher acquisitions are 60% rentals — does the K% trajectory effect even apply over a half-season?
articles.honest_critique: The symmetry across quartiles is the cleanest finding in the five. No real critique on methodology.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Reweight our trade-deck construction toward receiver-side player-quality and org dev-fit, deprioritize leading with the FV ledger.
articles.what_is_missing: Their max_fv=0 for Cashman across 202 trades is an instrument coverage failure, not evidence prospects don't matter. Recompute restricted to trades that actually included a graded prospect.
articles.honest_critique: The 'payroll isn't the gap' conclusion is contaminated — see GM trade ranking critique.

articles.what_i_would_do_with_it: Marginally informs portfolio thinking. Doesn't change a single trade evaluation.
articles.what_is_missing: Awards are heavily right-tail rentals (Verlander, Scherzer types) — does the depth-penalty hold for high-leverage October players who were acquired specifically for the stretch?
articles.honest_critique: Aggregate-level finding with no postseason cut. Useless for a contender's October roster.

articles.what_is_missing: Stratify by trade archetype — rentals, salary-dumps, prospect-for-vet, vet-for-vet. Aggregating these is meaningless.
articles.honest_critique: Outcome variable is net-of-cost, which mechanically penalizes high-payroll acquirers, then they interpret that penalty as 'money isn't the gap.' The confound encodes the conclusion.

articles.what_is_missing: Effect size is 0.03-0.07 SD. Payroll robustness check explicitly 'not yet run.' Scatter plot is a market-size confound — NYY, LAD, ATL, TOR cluster top-right.
articles.honest_critique: Don't publish before you stratify by payroll. Premature.

cross_article_observations: Zero mention of postseason, luxury tax, agent/extension probability, or medicals anywhere in the five pieces. That's a tell about who the site is built for.
Receiver-side dollar surplus net of cost is the wrong objective for a $250M payroll. We optimize playoff probability × playoff revenue.
Rental vs multi-year acquisitions are treated identically. Different decisions, different math.
what_i_actually_want_to_read_next: Playoff-leverage surplus model — rerun V3 with outcome = playoff-probability × playoff-revenue, not regular-season dollar surplus.
Deadline-rental sub-model restricted to <1.5 yrs control — that's 60% of my trade volume.
Post-acquisition extension probability — when does the rental convert?
what_this_site_is_missing_entirely: Anything that treats high-payroll trades as a distinct decision problem
